questions.prompt: An aligned unit square is tiled with half-open squares of width 1/4, treating outer boundary consistently. How many tiles cover its area?
questions.feedback_wrong: Count the four tiles along each axis.
questions.solution: There are four times four, hence sixteen tiles.

questions.prompt: Synthetic readout inference task: occupied-cell counts 64,32,16 are reported at widths 1,2,4 on two finite layered detector representations. A colleague treats the straight log-log relation as proof of an intrinsic three-dimensional fractal. Critique this inference using competing geometric/readout hypotheses. Contrast a finite point-center representation with filled pixels, propose sensitivity controls, and explain why transverse regrouping with fixed layer pitch needs a stated definition. No real detector result or experiment approval is implied.
criteria: Distinguish finite scale slope from an epsilon-to-zero geometric limit, including the representation dependence of finite points versus filled pixels.
State at least two competing explanations and appropriate grid-origin, scale-window or readout-threshold/mask controls without claiming those effects were observed.
Explain transverse/longitudinal scale assumptions and restrict conclusions to the supplied synthetic representation; no ECAL result or research approval follows.
questions.tests: independent critique of finite detector scaling inference
questions.solution: A few finite-scale counts do not establish an asymptotic dimension. A finite collection of point centers has bounded occupied-box count, hence dimension zero; a union of positive-area filled pixels is a different mathematical object. Finite scale geometry and readout/representation choices are competing hypotheses. Test sensitivity to origin, scale window and declared threshold or masks before attributing a pattern to intrinsic geometry. The cited HCAL simulation coarsens transversely and includes a longitudinal term; its observable cannot be imported as an unqualified three-dimensional ECAL limit.

steps.say: Count occupied boxes at a stated width. The mathematical dimension is a limiting growth rate when that limit exists; a finite readout supplies only finitely many resolutions.

limits: This is an illustration, not evidence about the learner or a detector.
Mathematical inference: finitely many point centers have eventually bounded counts; finite-scale slopes alone do not prove a nonzero limiting dimension. Filled pixels define a different set.
The Ruan et al. source studies an HCAL simulation and transverse regrouping with a longitudinal term. It is not a measured result for the user's ECAL setup.
